{13} Say, [O Muhammad], to these people who deny your message and reject your call, a parable from which they may take a lesson and which may serve as an admonition to them, if they are granted success in goodness. The parable is the people of the town, what passed between them of denying God's messengers, and what befell them of His punishment and retribution. Had identifying that town been of any benefit, God would have specified it. Therefore, inquiring into this and similar matters is a form of over-exertion and speaking without knowledge. For this reason, when someone speaks about such matters, you find in him confusion, muddle and disagreement, with no settled conclusion, by which you know that the path of sound knowledge is to adhere to realities and to abandon inquiry into what has no benefit. Thereby the soul is purified and knowledge increases, whereas the ignorant person thinks that his knowledge increases by citing opinions for which there is neither evidence nor proof, and from which nothing results but the confusion of the mind and the habituation to doubtful matters. The point is that God made this town a parable for those addressed. ﴿When the messengers came to them﴾: from God, ordering them to worship God alone, to devote religion sincerely to Him, and forbidding them from polytheism and sins.

{14} ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third﴾; that is, We strengthened them with a third, so they became three messengers, out of God's care for them and to establish proof through the succession of messengers to them. ﴿And they said﴾ to them: ﴿Indeed, we are messengers to you.﴾

{15} They answered them with the reply that has remained well known among those who reject the call of the messengers. They said: ﴿You are but human beings like us﴾; that is, what has made you superior to us and singled you out over us?!
The messengers said to their peoples: "We are but human beings like you, but God bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants." ﴿And the Most Merciful has not sent down anything﴾; that is, they denied the generality of messengership, then they also denied those addressed by it, saying: ﴿You are but liars.﴾

{16} These three messengers said: ﴿Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you.﴾ Had we been liars, God would have exposed our disgrace and would have hastened punishment against us.

{17} ﴿And our duty is only the clear conveyance﴾; that is, the clear conveyance by which the matters required to be made clear become evident. As for anything beyond this, such as signs demanded as proposals, or the speed of punishment, it is not up to us. Our function, which is clear conveyance, we have performed and made clear to you. So if you are guided, it is your good fortune and success; and if you go astray, we have no part in the matter.

{18} The people of the town said to their messengers: ﴿Indeed, we consider you a bad omen﴾; that is, we have seen nothing but evil in your coming to us and your contact with us. This is among the most astonishing of wonders: that the one who came to them with the greatest blessing God bestows upon His servants and the greatest honour He grants them, and whose need for it is beyond every need, should be regarded as an omen of ill. He came with a state of evil which added to the evil they were already in, and they took him as an omen. But failure and lack of success do more harm to their possessor than his enemy does. Then they threatened them, saying: ﴿If you do not desist, we will surely stone you﴾; that is, we will certainly kill you by stoning, the most abominable of killings. ﴿And a painful punishment from us will surely touch you.﴾

{19} Their messengers said to them: ﴿Your omen is with you﴾: that is, what is with them of polytheism and evil, which necessitates the occurrence of what is disliked, retribution, and the loss of what is loved and of blessing. ﴿Is it because you have been reminded?﴾; that is, because we have reminded you of what is good for you and your welfare, do you say what you say to us? ﴿Rather, you are a people who exceed limits﴾: transgressing the bounds and being perverse in your speech. **Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 36, verses 33–36:**

{33} That is: {And a sign for them}, regarding the resurrection, the rising, and standing before God, may He be exalted, for judgment upon their deeds, is {the dead earth}. God sent down rain upon it and brought it to life after its death, {and We brought forth from it grain, so from it they eat}: from all kinds of crops and from all kinds of plants that their livestock eat.

{34} {And We placed therein}; that is, in that dead earth, {gardens}; that is, orchards containing many trees, especially palm trees and grapevines, which are the most noble of trees, {and We caused springs to gush forth therein}; that is, in the earth. We placed in the earth those trees, palm trees, and grapevines.

{35} {So that they may eat of its fruit}: as sustenance, fruit, condiment, and pleasure. {And} the case is that those fruits were {not made by their hands}: they had no craftsmanship or labor in them. They are only the workmanship of the Most Wise of judges and the Best of providers. Moreover, their hands did not produce them by cooking or otherwise; rather, God brought these fruits into being, not needing cooking or anything else, to be taken from their trees and eaten immediately. {Will they not then be grateful?}: to the One who bestowed these blessings upon them and lavished upon them of His generosity and kindness that by which the affairs of their religion and their worldly life are set right. Is not He who brought the earth to life after its death, causing crops and trees to grow in it, depositing in it delicious fruits, bringing forth that fruit from those branches, and causing the dry dead earth to gush with springs, able to bring the dead to life? Indeed, He is over all things capable.

{36} {Glorified is He who created all the pairs}; that is, all the kinds, {of what the earth grows}: He diversified within it kinds too numerous to count, {and of themselves}: He diversified them into male and female, and varied their creation, character, and outward and inward attributes, {and of that which they do not know}: of the creatures that have been created and are hidden from our knowledge, and of those that have not yet been created. Exalted is He above having a partner, a helper, an assistant, a minister, a spouse, a child, a namesake, a like, or an equal in His attributes of perfection and qualities of majesty, or that anything He wills could overpower Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 36, verses 37–40:

{37} That is: {And a sign for them}: of the sway of His will, the perfection of His power, and His giving life to the dead after their death, is {the night: We strip from it the day}; that is, We remove the great light that covers the earth, replacing it with darkness and settling the darkness in its place; {and behold, they are in darkness}.

{38} Likewise, We remove this darkness that has overspread and enveloped them, and We cause the sun to rise, and it lights up the horizons, and creatures spread out for their livelihoods and their interests. For this reason He said: {And the sun runs on to a resting place for it}; that is, it constantly runs toward a fixed place for itself, which Allah has decreed. It neither exceeds it nor falls short of it, and it has no control over itself and no disobedience against the power of Allah, the Exalted. {That is the decree of the Almighty}: the One who by His might arranged these great creations with the most perfect arrangement and the best order. {The All-Knowing}: the One who by His knowledge made them a means of benefit for His servants and a source of benefit for their religion and their worldly life.

{39} {And the moon—We have determined for it phases}: it passes through them, one phase each night, {until}: it becomes very small and returns {like the old withered date-stalk}; that is, the stalk of the date palm which, once it has aged, dries out, shrinks in size and bends. Then after that it continues to increase little by little until its light is complete and its brightness is perfected.

{40} Each of the sun, the moon, the night and the day has been decreed by Allah in a measure that it does not exceed, and each has its authority and its time; when one comes into existence, the other ceases. For this reason He said: {It is not for the sun to overtake the moon}; that is, within its authority, which is the night; so it is impossible for the sun to appear during the night. {Nor does the night outstrip the day}: so that it enters before the end of its authority. {And each}: of the sun, the moon and the stars {in an orbit they swim}; that is, they move continuously. All of this is a clear proof and a dazzling demonstration of the greatness of the Creator and the greatness of His attributes, especially the attributes of power, wisdom and knowledge in this passage.

{41} That is: and a sign and proof for them that Allah alone is the one worthy of worship, because He is the Bestower of blessings and the Remover of calamities, and this is among His blessings: {that We carried their offspring}. Many commentators said: what is meant by this is their forefathers.

{42} {And We created for them} — that is, for those existing after them — {of the like of it} — that is, of the like of that ship, meaning its kind — {that which they ride}. Thus He mentioned His blessing upon the forefathers by carrying them in ships, because the blessing upon them is a blessing upon their offspring.

This passage is among the most difficult places for me in the interpretation. For what many commentators mentioned, that what is meant by the offspring is the forefathers, is not an established usage in the Qur'an, where the word "offspring" (dhurriyyah) is not applied to forefathers. Rather, it contains an ambiguity and takes the speech away from its proper subject, which the words of the Lord of the worlds, whose intent is clarity and explanation for His servants, would reject. There is a better possibility than this, namely that what is meant by "offspring" is the kind, and that they themselves are meant, because they are of the offspring of Adam's children. But this meaning is undermined by His saying: {And We created for them of the like of it that which they ride}. If it is meant: "And We created, from the like of that ship, for these addressed people, what they ride of the various kinds of ships," then this would be a repetition of meaning that the eloquence of the Qur'an would reject. If by His saying {And We created for them of the like of it that which they ride} is meant camels, which are the ships of the land, then the meaning is sound and clear; yet there remains some confusion in the speech. For if this meaning were intended, He would have said: "And a sign for them is that We carried them in the laden ship, and We created for them of its like that which they ride." Yet to say in the first: "We carried their offspring," and in the second: "We carried them," the meaning does not become apparent unless it is said that the pronoun refers to the offspring. And Allah knows the reality of the matter best.

When I reached this point in writing, a meaning became clear to me that is not far from the intent of Allah, the Exalted. That is, whoever knows the greatness of the Book of Allah and its complete clarification from every aspect of present, past, and future matters, and that it mentions from every meaning the highest and most complete of its states, and the ship has been among His signs and blessings upon His servants from the time He bestowed upon them the knowledge of it until the Day of Resurrection, and it has continued to exist in every age until the time of those addressed by the Qur'an. When Allah the Exalted addressed them with the Qur'an, and mentioned the state of the ship, and Allah the Exalted knew that the greatest signs of the ship would occur at other times and in other eras, when He teaches them the craft of the sea-going ships, both those with sails and those powered by fire, and the aerial ships that swim in the air like birds and the like, and land vehicles, in which the greatest sign was not found except in the offspring; He drew attention in the Book to the highest kind of its signs, saying: {And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship}; that is, the filled one with riders and goods. Thus Allah carried them and saved them, by the means that Allah taught them, from drowning.

{43} For this reason He reminded them of His blessing upon them, in that He saved them from drowning despite His power to do so, saying: {And if We will, We drown them, and there is no one to cry for them}; that is, no one to cry out for them so as to help them in their hardship and remove their distress, {nor are they rescued}, from what they are in.

{44} {Except as mercy from Us and enjoyment for a time}: in that We did not drown them, out of kindness to them and letting them enjoy for a time, perhaps they will return, or make up for what they neglected.

{45} {And when it is said to them: Fear what is before you and what is behind you}; that is, of the states of the barzakh and the Resurrection, and of the punishments in this world; {that perhaps you may receive mercy}: they turned away from that and did not raise their heads to it, even if every sign came to them.

{46} For this reason He said: {And no sign of the signs of their Lord comes to them but that they turn away from it}. The attribution of the signs to their Lord indicates their perfection and clarity, for nothing is clearer in its explanation of Allah's signs or greater in its clarity; and among the nurturing of Allah for His servants is that He delivered to them the signs by which they may be guided to what benefits them in their religion and their worldly life.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 36, verses 51–54:

{51} The first blast is the blast of terror and death. This is the blast of resurrection and rising up. When the Trumpet is blown, they will come forth {from the graves} {hastening} to their Lord; that is, they will hasten to be present before Him, unable to delay or hold back.

{52} In that state, the deniers will be grieved, will show regret and remorse, and will say: {"Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our resting place?"}; that is, from our sleep in the graves, for it has been reported in some hadiths that the people of the graves have a sleep just before the blowing of the Trumpet. They will be answered, and it will be said to them: {"This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth."}; that is, this is what Allah and the messengers promised you, and its truth will be seen with their own eyes. Do not think that the mention of "the Most Merciful" in this place is merely to report His promise; rather, it is to inform that on that great day they will see of His mercy what does not occur to thoughts nor enter the calculations of calculators, as in His saying: {"The dominion on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful"} and {"And voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful"}, and similar verses in which His name "the Most Merciful" is mentioned in this context.

{53} {"It will be but one cry"}: the raising from the graves will be only a single shout. Israfil will blow into the Trumpet, and bodies will come to life; {"and behold, they will all be brought before Us"}: the first and the last, both humankind and jinn, to be called to account for their deeds.

{54} {"So on that Day no soul will be wronged in anything"}: nothing will be taken away from its good deeds nor added to its evil deeds. {"And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do"}: whether good or evil. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame no one but himself.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 36, verses 55–58:

{55–56} When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that every person will be recompensed only for what they did, He mentioned the recompense of the two groups. He began with the recompense of the people of Paradise and informed that on that Day they will be {busy in enjoyment, reclining} (﴿إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ﴾); that is, in a preoccupation that delights the soul and gives it pleasure in everything that souls desire, that eyes find delightful, and that those who wish long for, and among that is the deflowering of beautiful virgins; as He said: {they and their spouses} (﴿هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ﴾), meaning the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn) who have combined beauty of face and body and beauty of character, {in shade, upon couches} (﴿فِي ظِلَالٍ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾), that is, adorned thrones decorated with fine, embellished cloth, {reclining} (﴿مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾) upon them, reclining in a manner that indicates complete comfort, tranquility and pleasure.

{57} {For them therein is fruit} (﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ﴾): abundant, from all kinds of delicious fruits, such as grapes, figs, pomegranates and others, {and for them is whatever they call for} (﴿وَلَهُمْ مَا يَدَّعُونَ﴾); that is, whatever they ask for. Whatever they request and wish for, they attain.

{58} And for them also is {peace} (﴿سَلَامٌ﴾), attained by them, {from a Lord, Most Merciful} (﴿قَوْلًا مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ﴾). In this is the speech of the Lord, the Exalted, to the people of Paradise and His peace upon them, and He emphasized it with His saying: {a word} (﴿قَوْلًا﴾). When the Lord, the Most Merciful, greets them with peace, they attain complete safety from every aspect, and they attain a greeting higher than which there is no greeting and the like of which there is no bliss. So what do you think of the greeting of the King of kings, the Great Lord, the Kind, the Merciful, to the people of the abode of His honour, those upon whom He has caused His good pleasure to descend, so He will never be displeased with them? Were it not that Allah, the Exalted, has decreed that they will not die, or that their hearts would not leave their places from joy, happiness and delight, that would have occurred. So we hope of our Lord that He does not deprive us of that bliss, and that He grants us enjoyment of gazing upon His Noble Face.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 36, verses 55–58:

{55–56} When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that every person will be recompensed only for what they did, He mentioned the recompense of the two groups. He began with the recompense of the people of Paradise and informed that on that Day they will be {busy in enjoyment, reclining} (﴿إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ﴾); that is, in a preoccupation that delights the soul and gives it pleasure in everything that souls desire, that eyes find delightful, and that those who wish long for, and among that is the deflowering of beautiful virgins; as He said: {they and their spouses} (﴿هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ﴾), meaning the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn) who have combined beauty of face and body and beauty of character, {in shade, upon couches} (﴿فِي ظِلَالٍ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾), that is, adorned thrones decorated with fine, embellished cloth, {reclining} (﴿مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾) upon them, reclining in a manner that indicates complete comfort, tranquility and pleasure.

{57} {For them therein is fruit} (﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ﴾): abundant, from all kinds of delicious fruits, such as grapes, figs, pomegranates and others, {and for them is whatever they call for} (﴿وَلَهُمْ مَا يَدَّعُونَ﴾); that is, whatever they ask for. Whatever they request and wish for, they attain.

{58} And for them also is {peace} (﴿سَلَامٌ﴾), attained by them, {from a Lord, Most Merciful} (﴿قَوْلًا مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ﴾). In this is the speech of the Lord, the Exalted, to the people of Paradise and His peace upon them, and He emphasized it with His saying: {a word} (﴿قَوْلًا﴾). When the Lord, the Most Merciful, greets them with peace, they attain complete safety from every aspect, and they attain a greeting higher than which there is no greeting and the like of which there is no bliss. So what do you think of the greeting of the King of kings, the Great Lord, the Kind, the Merciful, to the people of the abode of His honour, those upon whom He has caused His good pleasure to descend, so He will never be displeased with them? Were it not that Allah, the Exalted, has decreed that they will not die, or that their hearts would not leave their places from joy, happiness and delight, that would have occurred. So we hope of our Lord that He does not deprive us of that bliss, and that He grants us enjoyment of gazing upon His Noble Face.

{59} When Almighty God mentioned the reward of the righteous, He mentioned the reward of the criminals: that it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection, {"Stand apart today, O criminals!"} That is, separate yourselves from the believers and stand alone, so that He may rebuke and reproach them before all witnesses before He casts them into the Fire. He will say to them:

{60} {"Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?"} That is, did I not command and enjoin you through the tongues of My messengers and say to you: do not obey him! This rebuke encompasses all kinds of disbelief and disobedience, for they are all obedience to Satan and worship of him. {"Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy."} I warned you in the strongest terms against him, I informed you of his enmity, and I told you of what he calls you to.

{61} {"And that you should worship Me? This is a straight path."} That is, I commanded you to worship Me by carrying out My commands and abandoning what I forbade. {"This"}, that is, My worship, My obedience, and disobeying Satan, {"is a straight path."} The sciences of the straight path and its deeds return to these two matters. You did not keep My covenant nor act upon My instruction, and so you befriended your enemy.

{62} {"And he had already led astray a great multitude from among you."} That is, a great number of creatures. {"Did you not then understand?"} That is, did you not have intellect that would command you to take your Lord and true Protector as your ally, and restrain you from taking the greatest of enemies as your friend? Had you possessed sound intellect, you would not have done this.

{63} {"So when you obeyed Satan, opposed the Most Merciful, denied His meeting, and came to the Day of Resurrection, the abode of recompense, and the word of punishment was justified against you, [it will be said], 'This is Hell which you were promised,'"} the one you used to deny. {"Look at it now with your own eyes!"} There hearts will be struck with terror, eyes will be dazed, and the greatest terror will take hold.

{64} Then this is completed by commanding that they be taken to the Fire, and it will be said to them: {"Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve."} That is, enter it in a manner that its heat burns you, surrounds you, and reaches you to the utmost, because of your disbelief in God's signs and your denial of God's messengers.

{65} Almighty God said, describing their dreadful state in the abode of misery: {"Today We will seal their mouths,"} by making them mute so that they cannot speak, and so they will be unable to deny what they did of disbelief and denial. {"And their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn."} That is, their limbs will testify against them to what they did, and He who made everything speak will make them speak.

{66} {"And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes,"} by taking away their sight just as We sealed their speech. {"So they would race to the path,"} that is, hasten toward it, for it is the way to reach Paradise. {"But how could they see?"} For their eyes have been obliterated!

{67} {"And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places,"} that is, We would have taken away their movement, {"so they would not be able to proceed,"} forward, {"nor return"} backward, so that they might move away from the Fire.

The meaning is: these disbelievers have been justly subjected to the word of punishment, and there was no escape from their punishment. In that place there is nothing but the Fire, which has been made manifest, and no one has salvation except by crossing the Path. This can be done only by the people of faith who walk in their light. As for these people, they have no covenant with God regarding salvation from the Fire. Thus, if He wills, He obliterates their eyes and leaves their movement, so they cannot find the Path even if they race toward it and hasten to it; and if He wills, He takes away their motion, so they cannot advance or retreat. The point is that they will not cross it, and so salvation will not be attained for them.

{60} {"Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?"} That is, did I not command and enjoin you through the tongues of My messengers and say to you: do not obey him! This rebuke encompasses all kinds of disbelief and disobedience, for they are all obedience to Satan and worship of him. {"Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy."} I warned you in the strongest terms against him, I informed you of his enmity, and I told you of what he calls you to.

{61} {"And that you should worship Me? This is a straight path."} That is, I commanded you to worship Me by carrying out My commands and abandoning what I forbade. {"This"}, that is, My worship, My obedience, and disobeying Satan, {"is a straight path."} The sciences of the straight path and its deeds return to these two matters. You did not keep My covenant nor act upon My instruction, and so you befriended your enemy.

{62} {"And he had already led astray a great multitude from among you."} That is, a great number of creatures. {"Did you not then understand?"} That is, did you not have intellect that would command you to take your Lord and true Protector as your ally, and restrain you from taking the greatest of enemies as your friend? Had you possessed sound intellect, you would not have done this.

{63} {"So when you obeyed Satan, opposed the Most Merciful, denied His meeting, and came to the Day of Resurrection, the abode of recompense, and the word of punishment was justified against you, [it will be said], 'This is Hell which you were promised,'"} the one you used to deny. {"Look at it now with your own eyes!"} There hearts will be struck with terror, eyes will be dazed, and the greatest terror will take hold.

{64} Then this is completed by commanding that they be taken to the Fire, and it will be said to them: {"Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve."} That is, enter it in a manner that its heat burns you, surrounds you, and reaches you to the utmost, because of your disbelief in God's signs and your denial of God's messengers.

{65} Almighty God said, describing their dreadful state in the abode of misery: {"Today We will seal their mouths,"} by making them mute so that they cannot speak, and so they will be unable to deny what they did of disbelief and denial. {"And their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn."} That is, their limbs will testify against them to what they did, and He who made everything speak will make them speak.

{66} {"And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes,"} by taking away their sight just as We sealed their speech. {"So they would race to the path,"} that is, hasten toward it, for it is the way to reach Paradise. {"But how could they see?"} For their eyes have been obliterated!

{67} {"And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places,"} that is, We would have taken away their movement, {"so they would not be able to proceed,"} forward, {"nor return"} backward, so that they might move away from the Fire.

The meaning is: these disbelievers have been justly subjected to the word of punishment, and there was no escape from their punishment. In that place there is nothing but the Fire, which has been made manifest, and no one has salvation except by crossing the Path. This can be done only by the people of faith who walk in their light. As for these people, they have no covenant with God regarding salvation from the Fire. Thus, if He wills, He obliterates their eyes and leaves their movement, so they cannot find the Path even if they race toward it and hasten to it; and if He wills, He takes away their motion, so they cannot advance or retreat. The point is that they will not cross it, and so salvation will not be attained for them.

Allah, the Exalted, says: {And whomever We grant long life}: from among the children of Adam, {We reverse him in creation}; that is, he returns to the state from which he began, the state of weakness, weakness of intellect and weakness of strength. {Will they not then reason}: that the son of Adam is deficient in every respect, so that they would make up for their strength and their intellects, and employ them in obedience to their Lord?

{69} Exalted is He, He absolves His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) of what the polytheists accused him of, namely that he is a poet and that what he brought is poetry. So He says: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾ — that is, it is impossible that he should be a poet, because he is rightly guided and upon guidance, whereas poets are misguided, and "the misguided follow them." Moreover, Allah has cut off all the doubts by which the misguided hold on against His Messenger: He has precluded that he could write or read, and He informed us that He did not teach him poetry and that it is not befitting for him. ﴿It is but a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ — that is, what he brought is nothing but a reminder by which those of understanding remember all the religious matters; it comprises them in the most complete comprehension, and it reminds minds of what Allah has placed in their natures regarding the command to every good and the prohibition of every evil. ﴿And a clear Qur'an﴾ — that is, it makes clear what needs to be made clear. For this reason the object was omitted, to indicate that it makes clear all the truth with its detailed and summary proofs, and the falsehood along with the proofs of its invalidity. Allah sent it down thus to His Messenger.

{70} ﴿That he may warn whoever is alive﴾ — that is, whoever is living of heart and attentive; it is he who flourishes through this Qur'an, who increases in knowledge and action from it, and for whom the Qur'an is like rain to good, fertile land. ﴿And the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ — because the proof of Allah has been established against them through it, and their argument has been cut off, so no slightest excuse or doubt remains for them by which they could plead.

Ibn Sa'di says of verses 71–73: God, exalted is He, commands His servants to reflect upon the livestock (al-an'am) that He has subjected and made submissive for them, and has made them owners of these animals, which obey them in every matter they desire from them. He has placed in them many benefits: they carry them and their burdens, their saddles and their goods, from one place to another; they eat from them; in them is warmth (dif'); and from their wool, their fleece and their hair they obtain furnishings (athath) and provisions (mata') for a time. In them are also adornment and beauty, and other visible benefits from them.

{Will they not then be thankful?} to God, exalted is He, who has bestowed these blessings, and sincerely devote worship to Him alone, and not enjoy these things in a manner empty of reflection and contemplation?!

{74–75} This is an explanation of the falsehood of the gods of the polytheists, which they took besides Allah, hoping for their help and intercession; for they are utterly powerless. ﴿They cannot help them﴾: nor can they help themselves. So if they cannot help them, how could they help them?! Help requires two conditions: capability (istita'ah) [and power (qudrah)]. If one has the capability, there remains the question of whether he wants to help his servant or not. Thus, the negation of capability negates both matters together. ﴿And they are a host brought before them﴾; that is, they themselves are brought forward while they are in punishment, and some of them disavow others. Would that they had disavowed the worship of these in the world and devoted their worship to the One in whose hand is the dominion, benefit and harm, giving and withholding, and who is the Protector, the Helper!?

{76} That is: O Messenger, do not let the speech of the deniers grieve you. What is meant by "speech" is what the context indicates: every statement by which they disparage the Messenger or what he brought. That is, do not occupy your heart with grief over them. {Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal}; so We will recompense them according to Our knowledge of them. Otherwise, their speech does not harm you in the least.

These noble verses contain mention of the doubt of those who deny the Resurrection (ba'th) and the answer to it, in the most complete, best and clearest of answers.

{77} Then He, exalted is He, said: {Has not man considered}, the one who denies resurrection or doubts it, that He created him {from a sperm-drop}, and then moved him through the stages gradually, little by little, until he grew up, reached maturity, and his intellect became complete and firm. {Then he is an open adversary}, after having begun his creation from a sperm-drop. Let him consider the difference between these two states, and let him know that the One who originated him from nothing is able, all the more so, to restore him after he has been scattered and torn apart.

{78} {And he has presented for Us an example}, which no one should set forth, namely, measuring the power of the Creator by the power of the created, and holding that what is far-fetched for the power of the created is far-fetched for the power of the Creator. He explained this example with His saying: {He said}, that man: {"Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"}; that is, is there anyone who can give them life? This is a rhetorical question of denial; that is, no one can give them life after they have decayed and dissolved. This is the basis of the doubt and the example: that this is a matter utterly remote from what is known of human power. This statement that came from this man was heedlessness and forgetfulness of the beginning of his creation. Had he reflected upon his creation, after having been nothing worth mentioning, and then coming into existence before his eyes, he would not have set forth this example.

{79} Then Allah, exalted is He, answered this far-fetched claim with a sufficient and conclusive answer, saying: {Say, "He will give them life who brought them into being the first time."}: merely by conceiving this, one knows with certain knowledge, free of any doubt, that the One who originated them the first time is able to bring them back a second time, and that this is even easier for power when the one who contemplates it conceives it. {And He is Knowing of every creation}: this is also a second proof from the attributes of Allah, exalted is He, namely, that His knowledge encompasses all His creatures in all their conditions, at all times, and He knows what the earth diminishes of the bodies of the dead and what remains, and He knows the unseen and the witnessed. When the servant acknowledges this great knowledge, he knows that He is greater and more exalted than the reviving of the dead from their graves.

{80} Then He mentioned a third proof, saying: {He who has made for you from the green tree fire, and thereupon you ignite}: when He brings forth dry fire from the green tree, which is extremely moist, despite their opposition and great contrariness, then bringing forth the dead from their graves is similar to that.

{81} Then He mentioned a fourth proof, saying: {Is not He who created the heavens and the earth}: despite their vastness and magnitude, {able to create the like of them?}; that is, to restore them in their very selves. {Yes}: He is able to do that, for the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. {And He is the Creator, the Knowing}: this is a fifth proof, for He, exalted is He, is the Creator of all creatures, the first and the last, the small and the great; all of them are a trace of the traces of His creation and His power, and nothing that He wills to create is beyond His reach. Thus, restoring the dead is one instance among the instances of His creative works.

{82} For this reason He said: {His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is}: the indefinite noun in the conditional context encompasses everything, {that He says to it, "Be," and it is}; that is, immediately, without any hindrance.

{83} {So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things}: this is a sixth proof, for He, exalted is He, is the King, the Owner of all things, to whom belongs everything that dwells in the upper and lower world, and they are servants, subjugated and managed. He disposes of them by His decrees of destiny, His legislative rulings, and His rulings of recompense. Therefore, His restoring them after their death, so that the judgment of recompense may be carried out upon them, is part of the completeness of His dominion. For this reason He said: {And to Him you will be returned}, without any doubt or uncertainty, given the abundance of decisive proofs and manifest evidences for this. {Blessed is He who placed in His speech guidance, healing, and light.}

The commentary on Surah Yasin is complete.
So to Allah, exalted is He, belongs praise as befits His majesty, and to Him belongs thanks as befits His perfection, and to Him belongs glory as His greatness and magnificence require, and may Allah bless and grant peace to Muhammad (ﷺ).

{80} Then He mentioned a third proof, saying: {He who has made for you from the green tree fire, and thereupon you ignite}: when He brings forth dry fire from the green tree, which is extremely moist, despite their opposition and great contrariness, then bringing forth the dead from their graves is similar to that.

{81} Then He mentioned a fourth proof, saying: {Is not He who created the heavens and the earth}: despite their vastness and magnitude, {able to create the like of them?}; that is, to restore them in their very selves. {Yes}: He is able to do that, for the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. {And He is the Creator, the Knowing}: this is a fifth proof, for He, exalted is He, is the Creator of all creatures, the first and the last, the small and the great; all of them are a trace of the traces of His creation and His power, and nothing that He wills to create is beyond His reach. Thus, restoring the dead is one instance among the instances of His creative works.

{82} For this reason He said: {His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is}: the indefinite noun in the conditional context encompasses everything, {that He says to it, "Be," and it is}; that is, immediately, without any hindrance.

{83} {So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things}: this is a sixth proof, for He, exalted is He, is the King, the Owner of all things, to whom belongs everything that dwells in the upper and lower world, and they are servants, subjugated and managed. He disposes of them by His decrees of destiny, His legislative rulings, and His rulings of recompense. Therefore, His restoring them after their death, so that the judgment of recompense may be carried out upon them, is part of the completeness of His dominion. For this reason He said: {And to Him you will be returned}, without any doubt or uncertainty, given the abundance of decisive proofs and manifest evidences for this. {Blessed is He who placed in His speech guidance, healing, and light.}

The commentary on Surah Yasin is complete.
So to Allah, exalted is He, belongs praise as befits His majesty, and to Him belongs thanks as befits His perfection, and to Him belongs glory as His greatness and magnificence require, and may Allah bless and grant peace to Muhammad (ﷺ).
